title: Mixed-Linker Modification of MIL-100(Fe): Structure–Performance Trade-Offs in CO2 Adsorption and Cycling
abstract: Amine groups are often added to metal–organic frameworks to strengthen CO2 binding, usually at a cost in porosity. We examine this trade-off in MIL-100(Fe) prepared by a fluoride-free hydrothermal route, with 5, 10 or 20 mol% of the trimesate linker in the synthesis replaced by the amine-bearing linker 5-aminoisophthalic acid (AIA). Diffraction showed that the MIL-100 framework was retained and spectroscopy detected amine-related groups, although AIA incorporation was not quantified. Increasing AIA content reduced crystallite size from 43 to 18 nm and BET surface area from 1527 to 435 m2 g-1.

title: CelluloseForge: Crystallography-first construction of cellulose systems for molecular simulation
abstract: CelluloseForge is an open-source Python package for reproducibly constructing atomistic crystalline cellulose models. It represents experimental unit-cell data separately from molecular-mechanics parameters and generates unit cells, periodic bulk crystals, chain-parallel slabs for four cellulose allomorphs, and literature-defined 36-chain fibrils. Finite and covalently periodic chains can be parameterized with GLYCAM06j-1 or CHARMM36 and exported as matched GROMACS coordinates and topology.

title: Guidelines for minimizing contamination from Ag-based reference electrodes in aqueous and non-aqueous solvents
Assessment of honey samples from Nigerian markets using FTIR spectroscopy and machine learning
abstract: Honey adulteration with cheaper sugars is a concern in Nigerian markets, where conventional tests are slow, costly, and not widely accessible. This study assessed whether Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy combined with machine learning can screen honey for added sugar, and whether such a model can be applied to honey sold in Nigerian markets. A Random Forest classifier was trained on a public FTIR dataset of 16 honeys, each measured pure and with 10, 20, and 40% added sugar. It was compared with PLS-DA, logistic regression, and a support vector machine.

title: A neural surrogate for the natural-gas compressibility factor: reference-equation accuracy from synthetic training data alone, benchmarked on 2426 independent laboratory measurements
abstract: The compressibility factor z of natural gas is obtained either from inexpensive empirical correlations or from reference equations of state that require the full molar composition and an iterative density solve. Machine learning has been proposed as a bridge, but almost all published studies are trained and tested on values digitised from the same 1942 chart, so their gains have never been shown on independent laboratory data.

title: LearnM8: A Simple and Modular Molecular Active Learning Framework for any Oracle
abstract: Make-on-demand chemical spaces contain more than 10 11 compounds, which makes exhaustive virtual screening by docking or another costly scoring method (the oracle) impractical. Active learning reduces this cost by training a surrogate model (learner) on labeled compounds and using an acquisition strategy to select the next batch to evaluate. However, available implementations are built around particular docking programs and need new code for each oracle, learner and acquisition strategy.

title: Decoding Ionic Liquid Architecture at the Electrode-Electrolyte Interface in Supercapacitors.
abstract: The increasing demand for efficient energy storage underscores the need to enhance the capacity of electric double-layer capacitors (EDLCs), with electrolyte modification being a promising approach to improve their performance. Ionic liquids offer wide electrochemical stability windows, low volatility, thermal stability, and tunable molecular architectures, making them promising electrolytes for EDLCs.

title: Late-Stage 4-Methylation of [6,5]-Fused Arenes
abstract: Late-stage methylation of [6,5]-fused bicyclic arenes is a transformation of considerable importance in medicinal chemistry, yet the selective C4-methylation of these privileged scaffolds without directing groups has remained elusive. Here we report a relay strategy for the late-stage 4-methylation of [6,5]-fused arenes that couples temporary C3 iodination with a Catellani-type peri-methylation/ipso-H-termination sequence proceeding through an unusual six-membered palladacycle.

title: The liquid-gas equilibrium region for the quantum-volume Bragg-Williams equation of state
abstract: The quantum-volume Bragg-Williams (qv-BW) equation of state, derived from a lattice gas model and a mean-field approximation for the intermolecular interactions, includes a unique temperature dependence theoretically grounded through the connection to the thermal wavelength for particles. Here, the qv-BW equation of state is extended by deriving equations in a semi-analytical approach (one numerical inversion) for the two-phase region describing the liquid-gas equilibrium below the critical temperature.

title: Stochastic combinatorics with tripeptide dimers: finding the rational outcomes of extended games with structural fluctuations
abstract: While protein- and DNA-based macromolecular systems have previously been used to implement the solutions of certain combinatorial problems, similar progress using small organic molecules has been slow. In this paper, we deploy atomistic simulations to show that the structural fluctuations of the dimers of the tripeptide ProPhePhe (Pro = proline, Phe = phenylalanine) can be used to find the rational outcomes of a special class of extended games.

title: A Multi-Criteria Analytical Framework for the Assignment of Carboxyl-Rich Alicyclic Molecules in Dissolved Organic Matter
abstract: Dissolved organic matter (DOM) is one of Earth’s major organic carbon reservoirs, with most of this pool persisting as recalcitrant DOM (RDOM) over millennia-long timescales. However, the actual molecular structures within this recalcitrant pool remain poorly defined. Carboxyl-rich alicyclic molecules (CRAM) are widely used as molecular proxies for a portion of RDOM, but their assignment commonly relies only on elemental formula boundaries in direct-infusion mass spectrometry (MS) data, which cannot identify structural features or differentiate between isomers with different reactivities.

title: Implementation of fully automated continuous serial electron diffraction in Instamatic
abstract: Serial electron diffraction, especially when coupled with precession, utilises transmission electron microscopes to reveal crystal structures of beam-sensitive nanocrystals. Unfortunately, its application remains limited due to a lack of a transferable implementation. To address this issue, we added a new data collection protocol to the popular open-source software Instamatic. Utilising a static beam and continuous stage-sliding strategy, the new approach is well suited for high-throughput acquisition across a wide range of supported hardware.

title: MolValenceX: a browser-based, client-side tool for drawing molecules and estimating aromaticity, CIP stereodescriptors, dipole moments and Hansen solubility parameters, with benchmarking against experimental and reference-toolkit data
abstract: MolValenceX is a free, open-source chemical structure editor and analyser that runs entirely in a web browser, with no installation, server or account. A drawn or imported (SMILES) structure is analysed for molecular formula, molar mass and degree of unsaturation, ring aromaticity by Hückel π-electron counting, R/S configuration with optical-activity assessment from Cahn–Ingold–Prelog (CIP) priorities, E/Z configuration of acyclic double bonds, an empirical bond-moment estimate of the dipole moment from a generated 3D geometry, and Hansen solubility parameters (HSP) with a ranked…

title: Computational Insights into Chiral Induced Spin Selectivity in Organic Semiconductors via Circular Dichroism Prediction
abstract: Due to implications ranging from the origins of chirality in nature to the development of better spintronic devices, there is notable interest in gaining a deeper understanding of the quantum structure property relationships underlying the chiral induced spin-selectivity (CISS) effect. Although many features proposed to contribute heavily to CISS are computationally expensive, studies have shown that the maximum circular dichroism (CD) absorbance correlates strongly with the magnitude of CISS effect exhibited by a material and that time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) methods can…

title: Electrodes as Tunable Ligands: Electro-Inductive Control of Supported Catalyst Reactivity
abstract: Electronic tuning of molecular catalysts traditionally relies on synthetic modification of ligand structures, with each modification requiring the preparation of a distinct catalyst whose electronic properties are largely fixed at synthesis. Herein, we investigate a complementary strategy in which applied potential serves as a continuously adjustable electronic input to a surface-bound molecular catalyst.

title: FLAME: Fluorinated-motif Learning and Attribution for Molecular Explainability Applied to PFAS
abstract: Machine-learning (ML) architectures such as graph neural networks (GNNs) are increasingly used in structure-property modeling and molecular property prediction in fields of emerging contaminants such as per-and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS). However, their black-box nature makes these models difficult to use in scientific interpretation, decision making and in providing identifiable molecular substructures that contributed to the predictions.

title: Differentiable Search of Compositionally Complex Alloys
abstract: Identifying solid-solution compositions in multicomponent alloys requires exploring a highdimensional design space while accounting for competing phases. We present a differentiable search framework that uses composition gradients of a thermodynamic objective to identify promising alloy regions without exhaustive grid enumeration. In the present implementation, an alchemical machine-learning interatomic potential and ideal configurational entropy provide a differentiable free-energy approximation for random solid solutions.

title: Optical Properties of Monocarboxylic and Dicarboxylic Acids in the Atmosphere
abstract: The optical properties of atmospherically relevant molecular clusters remain elusive, as they are difficult to measure using current experimental techniques. Using quantum chemical methods, we here investigate the absorption and scattering properties of selective organic acid clusters. We studied 185 different (acid) 1 (Na + ) 0−2 (Cl – ) 0−1 (w) 0−5 clusters comprised of the monocarboxylic acids: Pyruvic acid (PA), lactic acid (LA), propionic acid (ProA), and 2,2-dihydroxypropionic acid (diol) and the dicarboxylic acids: Fumaric acid (FA) and maleic acid (MA).

title: Adsorption fingerprints of proteins at fluid interfaces: a molecular dynamics study of Lysozyme at water/oil and water/air interfaces
abstract: Protein adsorption at fluid interfaces is central to pharmaceutical formulation, food colloids, and bioprocessing technologies, yet its molecular basis remains poorly understood. We investigate lysozyme (LSZ) adsorption at water-air and water-hexadecane interfaces using molecular dynamics simulations with the all-atom CHARMM36m, united-atom GROMOS53A6, and coarse-grained MARTINI 3 force fields.

title: MeCoBi: A fast and accurate transition metal complex builder that generates 3D structures at scale and enables structure-based machine learning
abstract: The three-dimensional arrangement of ligands around a metal centre determines its electronic structure, reactivity, and biological activity, yet generating accurate three-dimensional (3D) structures from a ligand list remains difficult. Existing tools tend to be slow, narrow in coverage, or require manual specification. We present MeCoBi (Metal Complex Builder), an automated pipeline that builds and optimises 3D structures of mononuclear metal complexes from ligand SMILES across 36 d-block and main-group metals and coordination numbers 2–9.

title: Photovoltaic e-waste for PFAS remediation and H 2 evolution
abstract: End-of-life photovoltaic modules and persistent fluorinated compounds present distinct challenges for waste management and chemical recovery. Here, we report an integrated approach that uses silicon recovered from discarded photovoltaic modules to promote the mechanochemical defluorination of perand polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS). Subsequent alkaline treatment releases the retained fluorine as fluoride and generates hydrogen through oxidation of the remaining silicon, with SiO 2 as a third recoverable product.

title: Enantioselective Cobalt-Catalyzed Enyne Cyclo-1,4-Dienylation: Reaction Development and Mechanism
abstract: Cheap-metal-catalyzed asymmetric enyne cycloisomerizations that directly synthesize 1,4-dienes, named here as enyne cyclo-1,4-dienylation (abbreviated as cyclodienylation), remain scarce. The existing methods are largely limited to racemic transformations and mostly for 1,6-enynes. Here, we report a cobalt-catalyzed asymmetric enyne cyclo-1,4-dienylation using both 1,6-enynes and 1,7-enynes, delivering enantioenriched five- and six-membered rings bearing 1,4-diene moieties.

title: Development and Evaluation of an Agentic Suite of Tasks Covering a Computational Chemistry Curriculum
abstract: Computational chemistry, increasingly enabled by high-performance computing, accelerates research across many areas of chemistry. However, heterogeneous software packages, input formats, and output conventions create a steep learning curve that also complicates simulation scripting and automation. Large language models (LLMs) can lower this barrier by helping users prepare calculations, execute workflows, and interpret results. We present ASSAY (Agentic Simulation Suite for Automated Chemistry), an open-source agentic toolkit for quantum chemistry designed for undergraduate CC education.

title: Assessing the predictive limits of machine learning on cyclic peptides
abstract: Machine learning (ML) has become a key tool in molecule discovery and optimization. Yet cyclic peptides, which occupy an intermediate chemical space between small molecules and proteins, have received limited attention in ML research, leaving the predictive value of current methods and future research needs unclear. To address this gap, we systematically evaluated ten model families (from classical ML approaches to pretrained deep-learning models) and nine molecular representations (from molecular descriptors to strings and graphs) across twelve prediction tasks spanning three properties and…

title: Intracellular fate of structurally heterogeneous carbon nitride structures in mammalian cells
abstract: Carbon nitride materials are increasingly investigated for photocatalysis, environmental remediation, and emerging biomedical applications. Although the biological behavior of carbon nitride quantum dots has been studied quite extensively, interactions of larger and structurally heterogeneous carbon nitride structures with cells remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate the intracellular fate of two carbon nitride samples possessing markedly different characteristic dimensions, spanning a range from approximately 100 nm to several micrometers.

title: A General Strategy for Active Learning When Predicting Reaction Performance in a Target Domain
abstract: Machine learning models can help guide reaction development, but their usefulness is often limited by the scarcity of training data in the chemical spaces where predictions are most needed. Active learning can reduce this burden by selecting a minimal number of maximally informative experiments. However, standard acquisition strategies such as Bayesian active learning by disagreement (BALD) prioritize uncertainty without regard to the specific prediction domain of interest.

title: Dual-Microcapsule-Triggered In Situ Polymerization Enables Ultralong Room-Temperature Phosphorescence for Damage Visualization and Dynamic Anti-Counterfeiting
abstract: 2 challenging because efficient triplet emission generally requires a rigid molecular environment that is difficult to establish in situ. Here, we report a dual-microcapsule strategy that activates ultralong RTP through damage-triggered in situ polymerization. Two complementary types of microcapsules, separately encapsulating an epoxy precursor and an amine solution containing organic phosphors, were incorporated into a coating.

title: A bespoke, token-efficient LLM inference pipeline for extracting polymer diffusion coefficients from scientific literature
abstract: Automated creation of actionable chemical datasets through large language model (LLM) interpretation of chemistry publications has become an engineering challenge rather than a frontier AI problem. We present Chemstractor , a bespoke extraction pipeline designed for use with open‑weight LLMs that can be executed locally on hardware typically available to university research environments. As a test case, the extraction techniques are applied to polymer diffusion coefficients, commonly used for the prediction of polymer molecular weights and for evaluating emerging universal calibration curves.

title: Chemistry-informed non-covalent graphs and pharmacophore supervision for molecular property prediction
abstract: Graph neural networks describe a molecule by its covalent bonds, however, many molecular properties are shaped by contacts between atoms that are not bonded to each other. Existing models either ignore these non-covalent interactions or approximate them with a distance cutoff that cannot distinguish an interaction from mere proximity. Here we introduce a framework that injects chemical knowledge at two levels.

title: Decoupled Semisolid Extrusion and Drop-on-Demand Dispensing for Liposomal Nanomedicine Tableting
abstract: Distributed manufacturing of personalized oral nanomedicines requires processing that protects delicate nanocarriers from thermal and mechanical degradation. Tableting of liposomal nanomedicine into solid dosage forms has gained interest by providing enhanced physicochemical stability and room temperature storage, simplifying cold-chain logistics. Nanomedicine advancements have corresponded with the recent push toward an agile decentralized manufacturing paradigm, incorporating additive manufacturing and 3D printing technologies.

title: From Local Motifs to Long-Range Order: Adaptive Diffusion of the Complex Au–S Surface Reconstruction
abstract: Surface reconstructions present a challenging structure-prediction problem because locally favorable atomic motifs must be accommodated within the periodicity of the underlying crystal, often producing large and complex surface unit cells. Here, we extend adaptive diffusion to jointly explore continuous atomic coordinates and discrete surface cell transformations, allowing favorable atomic arrangements and periodicities to be discovered together.

title: From Cell to Pack: Experimental Validation of a Thermo-Electrochemical 4s4p Battery Model
abstract: Growing deployment of lithium-ion batteries has intensified the need for advanced battery pack simulation tools to address the key engineering challenge of accurately predicting the electrical and thermal behaviour of battery packs. This work presents a scalable, physics-based simulation framework for arbitrary (Ms, Np) lithium-ion battery pack configurations. The framework is demonstrated and experimentally validated using a 4s4p pack with bottom cooling.

title: Hard X-ray Studio for reproducible analysis of static and modulated excitation X-ray absorption spectroscopy
abstract: Quick-scanning X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy (QXAFS) is an emerging technique recent year, which enables complete XAS to be acquired on sub-second to second timescales, providing a powerful means of probing transient electronic and local structural changes under operando conditions. We present Hard X-ray Studio, a local application combining a browser interface with a Python and XrayLarch service. Static mode prepares individual spectra or merges reviewed repeats into named conditions before feature extraction.

title: Integrated Computational Design and Multistage Virtual Screening for the Prioritization of Putative USP5 Catalytic-Cleft Inhibitors
abstract: Ubiquitin-specific protease 5 (USP5) processes unanchored polyubiquitin and has been linked to cancer-associated signaling. We developed a computer-aided workflow to generate and rank small molecules against its catalytic/substrate cleft. The starting dataset contained 26 activity records representing 19 unique compounds, ten with measured half-maximal inhibitory concentrations. Descriptor-based quantitative structure-activity relationship models underwent compound leave-one-out and scaffold-held-out validation.

title: 3-Methyl-2-Oxazolidinone (MOX), an Effective and Plausibly Green Solvent Replacement for DMF in Amidation Reactions
abstract: The solvent N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) is widely used in organic synthesis for a broad range of chemical reactions. However, prolonged exposure to DMF presents serious health hazards due to its hepatotoxicity and reproductive toxicity. Growing appreciation of these risks has motivated public and private institutions to phase out the use of DMF and identify safe, viable alternatives for various applications. This is especially urgent for amidation, the most frequently performed reaction class in pharmaceutical organic synthesis, for which DMF is the most frequently used solvent.

title: Oxygen-Driven Etching of MAX Phases Assisted by HF Vapor (OxyVap-HF) for MXenes Synthesis
abstract: MXenes are conventionally produced by immersing MAX phases in fluoride-containing acids, where removal of A elements proceeds via their proton-driven oxidation leading to H 2 gas evolution accompanied by fluoride complexation with A n+ . Here we introduce a different, oxygen-driven HF vapor assisted route (OxyVap-HF) in which a precursor MAX phase, such as Ti 3 AlC 2 , is held separated from a dilute HF solution reservoir and etched by oxygen available in air, assisted by HF/H 2 O vapor helping to maintain access of oxygen to A element layers.

title: Lorentz-Covariant Bi-Photonic Kinematics: Deriving Optical Polarization and the Born Rule from Internal Constrained Dynamics
abstract: (Dated: November 7, 2026) Standard quantum electrodynamics (QED) treats the photon as an unstructured, point-like excitation of a gauge field. In this orthodox framework, when light encounters a measurement device, its continuous wave description abruptly and unpredictably reduces to a single discrete detector click. The statistical likelihood of recording that click is calculated by squaring the overlap between the incoming wave state and the detector state—an operational prescription universally known as the Born rule (P = |⟨ϕ|ψ⟩|2).

title: On the real role of hydroxide in zeolite crystallization: electrochemically-generated OH synthesis
abstract: Hydrothermal synthesis of zeolites is typically conducted in basic media, where the hydroxide anion (OH - ) acts as a mineralizing agent, promoting the transformation of precursors into crystalline frameworks. OH - is introduced together with (in)organic structure-directing agents ((in)OSDAs), thus always accompanied by a counter-cation (e.g., Tetrapropylammonium + , Na + ). Consequently, for systems containing only monovalent ions, the OH - /SDA + ratio generally remains at 1 (or below).

title: Machine Learning-Guided Comparison of n- and p-Type Reorganization Energies
abstract: A key component in the rational design of novel, high-performing candidate organic electronic materials is understanding and predicting the charge transport properties of π-conjugated materials. Although purely experimental design methods can be prohibitively expensive, previous computational investigations have established cost-saving methods to accurately predict charge transport for π-conjugated materials via internal Marcus reorganization energy.

title: Absolute quantification and profiling of cellular tRNAs by nanopore sequencing and a deep learning classifier
abstract: Transfer RNAs (tRNAs) link mRNA codons to amino acids during translation. Their abundance and modification states are dynamically regulated and influence translation efficiency, mRNA stability, and proteostasis. Accurate profiling of tRNAs is essential, but deep sequencing suffers from modification-induced biases during cDNA synthesis, while nanopore direct RNA sequencing (DRS) still faces challenges in accurate tRNA profiling. Here, we develop an end-to-end deep learning model, termed nano tRNA classifier, that directly uses nanopore-DRS ionic current signals to classify tRNAs without basecalling. The model achieves 98.2% classification accuracy with high read retention across all Escherichia coli tRNA species. Using an equimolar mixture of native tRNAs as a ground-truth reference, we correct read-count bias, enabling absolute quantification and profiling under diverse culture conditions. We further develop binary classifiers that detect specific tRNA modifications at the single-molecule level with high accuracy. This nanopore-based platform integrates accurate tRNA classification, absolute quantification, and single-molecule modification detection.

title: Integrating ToF-SIMS and machine learning reveals a mammary tumor-associated multi-ion signature
abstract: Cancer biomarkers should be specific, reproducible, and accessible from practical biological samples. Although omics-based approaches have substantially advanced biomarker discovery, many strategies still rely on individual molecules or limited molecular panels, which may not fully capture the complexity of tumor biology. Whether tumor-associated chemical signatures can improve cancer detection remains an open question. Here, we investigated whether a breast tumor-associated multi-ion signature could be detected in mammary gland tissue from the MMTV-PyMT breast cancer mouse model, as well as in liver, serum, and fur collected from the same animals. Low-mass ions (m/z 50-250) were analyzed using time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (ToF-SIMS) combined with multivariate analysis and machine learning. A robust mammary tumor multi-ion signature reliably distinguished tumor-bearing from healthy mice, with both partial least squares-discriminant analysis (PLS-DA) and random forest achieving an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.997 under leave-one-animal-out cross-validation. Animal-label permutation testing confirmed that classification performance was significantly greater than expected by chance, and 98 of 313 ions differed significantly at the animal level. While liver and serum samples showed little evidence of tumor-associated discrimination, fur showed the highest classification performance and the greatest overlap in discriminative ions with mammary tissue. These findings demonstrate that low-mass ToF-SIMS enables robust identification of mammary tumor-associated multi-ion signatures, but that their detectability varies across biological matrices. Although the evidence in fur remained exploratory, it suggests that some tumor-associated chemical information may extend beyond the primary tumor and warrants further investigation of hair and related minimally invasive samples for cancer detection.

title: Data-Driven Design of Biofunctional Molecularly Imprinted Polymers for Precision Diagnostics
abstract: Conventional imprinted receptors design is laborious and reliant on trial-and-error experimentation. To overcome existing challenges, this study integrates molecular mechanics/molecular dynamics (MM/MD) and machine learning (ML) to design molecularly imprinted polymer nanoparticles (nanoMIPs), aiming to uncover synergies and gaps between physics-informed and data-driven approaches. By systematically comparing and experimentally evaluating MM/MD formulations with ML-predicted recipes, we establish a multimodal framework for cross-validation, method selection, and accelerated development of biomimetic materials for precision cancer diagnostics. A monomer library is screened using hybrid MM/MD method, leading to a generalizable nanoMIP formulation for detecting cancer biomarkers. In parallel, we introduce an ML algorithm that predicts nanoMIP formulations, reducing formulation prediction time for new epitopes from months of conventional computational/experimental screening to seconds after model training. Trained on epitope fragments, the ML framework supports epitope-mediated imprinting by generating recipes tailored to the physicochemical properties of targeted peptides. The curated dataset and integrated MM/MD-ML workflow developed in this study, capture molecular interactions beyond experimental reach, while experimental synthesis and evaluation ensure alignment between formulation predictions and nanoMIP performance under experimentally relevant conditions. This multimodal, feedback-loop-based framework improves predictive accuracy of imprinted polymer formulations, provides mechanistic insights, and supports hypothesis-guided design of advanced nanoMIPs.

title: GenEdXR: A Generative AI-Driven Extended Reality Framework for Adaptive Educational Entertainment Ecosystems
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence and extended reality (XR) offer unprecedented opportunities for adaptive educational entertainment, yet existing systems suffer from static content pipelines and weak integration between immersive interaction and intelligent adaptation. Here we introduce GenEdXR, a framework that unifies a transformer-based deep knowledge tracing (DKT) module, a large-language-model content synthesis pipeline, a proximal-policy-optimisation adaptive orchestration engine, and multi-modal XR rendering within a closed-loop architecture.

title: In Silico Design of Dimerization Interfaces in Drosophila melanogaster Glutathione Transferase
abstract: Understanding the molecular determinants of protein–protein interface stability remains a central challenge for the rational engineering of oligomeric enzymes. Here, the glutathione transferase GSTE3 from Drosophila melanogaster is used as a model system to decipher the factors governing dimer stability through an integrated structural, computational, and experimental approach. The X–ray crystal structure reveals a canonical homodimeric organization with a conserved Epsilon-class dimerization motif at the subunit interface.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Membrane Lipid Composition and Asymmetry Modulate Translocation Versus Leakage of the Model Amphipathic Peptide MAP
abstract: Cell-penetrating peptides (CPPs) can enable intracellular access while avoiding cytotoxicity, yet their behavior is highly sensitive to membrane composition. Here we show that lipid composition and leaflet asymmetry act as a switch that determines whether the amphipathic CPP MAP undergoes nondisruptive translocation or stabilizes membrane pores that drive leakage. Using high-field computational electrophysiology (CompEL) simulations in membranes of increasing physiological relevance, we show that electrically induced membrane defects allow the insertion of MAP peptides. We find symmetric anionic bilayers favor MAP insertion coupled to transmembrane pore stabilization in POPC/POPG membranes, reproducing progressive dye release in liposome leakage assays. Incorporation of cholesterol reduces the number of inserted peptides and conducts to faster leakage kinetics in cholesterol-containing vesicles. In contrast, a minimal asymmetric membrane model (POPC extracellular leaflet; POPC/POPS intracellular leaflet) supports MAP translocation without sustained membrane disruption. This delivery-relevant mechanism is supported by efficient MAP internalization in HEK293 cells while maintaining high viability. Polarized ATR–FTIR provides structural context, indicating predominantly membrane-associated α-helical conformations across lipid compositions. Together, these results establish lipid asymmetry and composition as actionable biointerface parameters that tune CPP function between translocation and leakage and demonstrate an experimentally benchmarked framework for predicting membrane outcomes across complex lipid environments.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Two Better Than One: Emerging Chirality in Twisted Gold Nanorods
abstract: Chemisorption-directed growth is the most common strategy for the synthesis of intrinsically chiral plasmonic nanoparticles. This approach relies on the use of thiolated chiral molecules, such as cysteine, which are assumed to transfer chirality by selectively adsorbing onto specific gold crystal facets during growth on preformed gold seeds. We found that chiral Au nanorods (AuNRs) synthesized using aged cysteine solutions exhibit significantly enhanced anisotropy factors compared to freshly prepared solutions, thus challenging the long-standing assumption of the key role of thiol ligands. Combining circular dichroism spectroscopy, electron tomography, and density functional theory simulations, we prove that cysteine is gradually oxidized into cystine and that this transformation is responsible for the enhanced chiroptical response. We therefore identify cystine, rather than cysteine, as the chiral inducer during AuNR chiral growth. Cystine’s ability to simultaneously coordinate two gold atoms enables a more efficient transfer of molecular chirality to the growing nanocrystal. This enhanced efficiency stems from its ability to directly fit the 3-point chirality model, thereby avoiding stochastic processes. These findings redefine the role of thiolated chiral molecules in chemisorption-directed growth and provide mechanistic insights for the rational design of more effective chirality inducers.

title: Electrostatic Presolvation Enables Selectivity in Photoinduced Ligand Exchange
abstract: Functional group compatibility remains a central challenge in photochemical C–H activation with metal complexes. Strongly donating groups preferentially coordinate to the reactive unsaturated metal and suppress weaker C–H coordination and σ-complex formation required for C–H bond activation. Controlling the initial coordination in photoinduced ligand exchange is therefore one approach to achieving selectivity in bond activation. Here, we resolve the elementary steps of photoinduced CO to acetonitrile ligand substitution for Rh(acac)(CO)2 with femtosecond-resolution X-ray absorption spectroscopy at the Rh L3-edge. We directly observe the formation of a hitherto undetected transient acetonitrile C–H σ-complex and its subsequent rearrangement to the thermodynamically favored nitrogen-coordinated solvent complex. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that the initial C–H coordination is enabled by electrostatic presolvation, which orients the acetonitrile methyl groups toward the metal center prior to CO dissociation. Our results point to a general strategy to direct selectivity in C–H activation by controlling coordination through presolvation.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Spin order steers a light–matter condensate
abstract: Light–matter condensates get a magnetic control knob. In the layered magnet CrSBr, reorienting the spins with a modest field shifts the condensate’s colour by more than 10 meV.

title: Programmable interphyla communication for Staphylococcus aureus by transferability of homoserine lactone sensors between Bacillales bacteria
abstract: Staphylococcus aureus is a Gram-positive opportunistic pathogen of the order Bacillales and a frequent member of human-associated microbiomes. Despite its clinical relevance, engineering S. aureus and the communities it inhabits remains limited by a shortage of well-characterized genetic tools for precise control of gene expression and intercellular signaling. Biosensors for homoserine lactones (HSLs) are widely used in Gram-negative bacteria, as HSLs are small, passively diffusible signaling molecules for and their sensors are tightly regulated. Here, we show that synthetically designed HSL sensors using LuxR-family regulators are highly functional in S. aureus. Notably, synthetic designs previously built for the Gram-positive model Bacillus subtilis, a distantly related Bacillales, transferred functionally and establish repurposing the genetic toolbox as an effective strategy for importing these functions into S. aureus. Sensor performance correlated strongly between the two Bacillales, and activation in S. aureus reached 55-fold, exceeding the dynamic range of reported inducible systems. We further demonstrate tightly regulated, programmable interphyla communication between Gram-negative Escherichia coli and S. aureus via HSL signaling. These results provide a new toolset for engineering interbacterial communication and open a route to extending programmable HSL signaling to other tough-to-engineer bacteria.

title: Modular assembly of mitochondrial complex III from a dynamic matrix domain pool
abstract: Mitochondrial complex III is a central component of the cellular energy metabolism. It is an obligate dimer of catalytic and accessory subunits that are encoded by two genomes. How its large matrix domain, formed by the core proteins Qcr1 and Qcr2, is built and joined to the membrane part and during assembly is not known. Here we show that Qcr1 and Qcr2 preassemble independently of complex III into matrix domain modules.

title: Vasopressin V2 receptor phosphopeptide reshapes the conformational landscape of arrestin-2 beyond C-tail detachment
abstract: Binding of phosphorylated GPCR tails influences arrestin conformation, but the contribution of this interaction to the interdomain rotation associated with activation remains incompletely characterised. In particular, it remains unclear whether displacement of the arrestin C-tail is sufficient to favor larger interdomain rotations or whether the bound phosphotail exerts an additional effect on the conformational landscape. Here, we used enhanced-sampling simulations to characterise the conformational free-energy landscapes of basal (unbound) and V2Rpp-bound arrestin-2. We find that V2Rpp binding broadened the range of energetically accessible interdomain rotation angles relative to basal arrestin-2. However, the pronounced rotation observed in the experimental structures, while accessible, was not strongly favored. Strikingly, C-tail displacement alone does not reproduce this effect, as arrestin-2 retains a strong preference for small interdomain rotation angles in the absence of V2Rpp. Moreover, the C-tail-detached state is energetically unfavorable in the absence of V2Rpp. Together, these findings quantify the effects of V2Rpp binding on the interdomain rotation of arrestin-2 and disentangle the effects of phosphopeptide binding from those of C-tail detachment.

title: Purple bacteria transform waste into valuable antioxidant
abstract: The colorful microbes can use carbon from waste products, instead of sugars, to make CoQ10 and carotenoid pigments

title: A hierarchical general video matting framework towards temporal coherence
abstract: Video Matting is the process of accurately extracting foreground objects from a sequence of input video frames, which requires the accurate estimation not only on the transparency of foreground objects for each frame but also on the spatial-temporal object coherence between consecutive frames. Meanwhile, the prevailing data-driven deep-learning based video matting approaches are constrained by fixed datasets and limited feature aggregation and filtering patterns, making it hard to guarantee the matting results in terms of coherence and accuracy, especially of general foreground objects.
