title: Catalytic Interphases Enable Sulfur Redox Catalysis in All-Solid-State Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
abstract: Weak solid–solid contact with limited chemical and transport continuity is a common bottleneck in solid-state batteries, particularly in all-solid-state lithium–sulfur batteries (ASSLSBs), where Li2S/S8 conversion requires catalytic acceleration but lacks a continuous solid-state catalytic pathway. Here, we propose an interphase catalysis strategy for solid–solid sulfur conversion by transforming discrete catalyst/reactant interfaces into a chemically integrated reaction interphase.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Catalytic Stereoselective Inverse Electron Demand Formal Aza-Diels–Alder: Access to Highly Congested Molecular Bowl-Shaped 3D Tertiary Amines
abstract: Diastereoselective sp3-rich heteroatom-based bowl-shaped polycyclic molecules are a key structural scaffold in various bioactive molecules. Due to the inherent steric congestion of these structures, achieving precise stereochemical control remains a significant challenge in contemporary synthetic chemistry. We herein disclose a practical iron-catalyzed assembly of an indole-derived tertiary amine-based pentacyclic molecule through an intermolecular, iminium-triggered dearomative inverse electron-demand formal aza-Diels–Alder (IEDFADA) reaction.

title: GeneEmbedLLM: Harnessing Large Language Models for Gene Functional Embedding and Association Prediction
abstract: 将上述摘要提取为连续文本如下： Effective and high-quality gene function representations are crucial for bioinformatics tasks. While biological knowledge about genes is inherently textual, encompassing functional descriptions and pathway annotations, current methods often rely on single-source, non-textual data, failing to capture the rich semantic information in multi-source gene annotations. In this paper, we propose GeneEmbedLLM, a Large Language Model (LLM)-powered framework for generating universal, semantically-aware gene embeddings.

title: Interventional breath analysis reveals oral microbial conversion of 1,2-Propanediol into Propanal and 1-Propanol
abstract: Background: Orally exhaled breath contains volatile organic compounds (VOCs) that may reflect local microbial metabolism as well as systemic processes. Consequently, the breath sampling route can influence VOC profiles and complicate biomarker interpretation. Previous studies have shown that 1-propanol is substantially enriched in orally compared with nasally exhaled breath. Objective: To determine whether a controlled oral challenge with 1,2-propanediol (1,2-PD) induces sampling route-dependent changes in breath 1-propanol concentrations. Methods: Ten healthy volunteers received 0.1 mL 1,2-PD diluted in approximately 50 mL water. The solution was used as an oral rinse for approximately 30 s and then expectorated. Matched oral and nasal end-tidal breath samples were collected before administration, immediately afterwards, and at 15-min intervals. Propanal, 1-propanol, acetol, acetone, and isoprene were analysed using gas chromatograph-ion mobility spectrometer (GC-IMS). Results: Oral 1,2-PD exposure produced a rapid and transient increase in exhaled propanal and 1-propanol signals, with the largest responses immediately after administration and at the second post-intervention measurement. In contrast, nasal signals remained comparatively stable. Acetone and isoprene showed no consistent intervention-related changes, regardless of the sampling route. No reproducible increase in acetol was detected, although interpretation was limited by analytical interference. Conclusion: A controlled oral 1,2-PD challenge elicited a route-specific propanal and 1-propanol response, consistent with local microbial metabolism of 1,2-PD within the oral cavity. Both fucose and 1,2-PD have been previously reported in human saliva, including elevated concentrations in selected disease-associated contexts. Bacteria can degrade salivary mucin glycans, releasing sugars including fucose. Together, these observations motivate investigation of a proposed pathway linking mucin-derived fucose to 1,2-PD and subsequent propanal and 1-propanol formation in the human oral cavity.

title: PCB-Exposed Gut Microbiota Recapitulate Neurobehavioral Deficits and Reprogram Hippocampal Transcriptomic Signatures
abstract: Polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) are persistent environmental pollutants associated with developmental neurotoxicity and autism spectrum disorder (ASD). However, whether PCB-induced alterations in gut microbiota contribute to neurodevelopmental toxicity independently of direct chemical exposure remains unclear. Here, we investigated whether transplantation of PCB-associated gut microbiota produces early neurobehavioral alterations and disrupts brain molecular pathways in offspring. Gut microbiota from conventional dams exposed to the Fox River PCB mixture (FRM; 6.0 mg/kg/day) or vehicle were transplanted into germ-free recipient females without direct PCB administration. At postnatal day 7 (P7), offspring underwent ultrasonic vocalization (USV) testing, whole-brain RNA sequencing (n = 4/sex/group), and untargeted serum metabolomics. Untargeted serum metabolomics were also performed in donor dams. PCB-associated fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) significantly reduced offspring USVs, reproducing effects observed following direct maternal PCB exposure. Brain transcriptomics in offspring identified substantially more differentially expressed genes in males (9,339) than females (1,082), including 512 shared genes. Concordantly regulated genes revealed downregulation of neurotransmitter signaling and ion channel pathways alongside upregulation of RNA processing pathways. Male-associated responses involved altered protein synthesis and neuronal signaling, whereas female-associated responses involved DNA repair and extracellular matrix remodeling. Despite these molecular differences, behavioral responses showed no significant sex-dependent effect. Maternal metabolomics revealed increased bile acids and decreased indole-3-propionic acid, highlighting potential AhR-NF{kappa}B and bile acid-associated signaling mechanisms. Offspring metabolomics further identified alterations in lipid-associated metabolites and metabolic profiles. Collectively, these findings show that transferring PCB-exposed microbiota reproduces early neurobehavioral alterations and induces shared and sex-biased molecular responses, identifying the maternal gut microbiome as a candidate mediator linking PCB exposure to developmental neurotoxicity.

title: X-Shaped Multichannel Conjugation Enabled by Excited-State Aromaticity
abstract: Molecular topology governs the photophysical properties of polycyclic π-conjugated systems by defining their effective conjugation pathways. Conventionally, linear π-extension is considered more effective than angular extension in increasing the effective conjugation length and narrowing the optical bandgap. Here we uncover an inverse topology–property relationship in π-extended dihydrophenazines (DHPs): linear extension unexpectedly blueshifts fluorescence, whereas angular extension produces pronounced redshifts.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: TABLNet: Trustworthy Adaptive Broad Learning Network for Physical-Layer Device Authenticationin Intelligent IoT Networks
abstract: Securing the expanding internet of things (IoT) ecosystem demands lightweightauthentication mechanisms compatible with hardware-constrained edge end-points. Specific emitter identification (SEI) exploits manufacturing-induced radiofrequency (RF) fingerprints to verify device identity at the physical layer, cir-cumventing the overhead of upper-layer cryptographic schemes. Nevertheless,contemporary deep generative architectures employed for automated RF fin-gerprint synthesis impose prohibitive computational demands that hinder theirdeployment on resource-limited platforms.

title: Maximizing the Photocatalytic Performance of Covalent Organic Frameworks by Decoupling Charge Separation and Recombination via Guest π-Conjugation
abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) have emerged as promising candidates for solar-driven photocatalysis; however, simultaneously achieving ultrafast electron–hole separation and suppressed charge recombination remains challenging. Here, we demonstrated a theory-guided design of high-performance host–guest COFs by tuning π-conjugation of embedded guest molecules.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: ProTEUS: A mutation-resolved world model for closed-loop protein evolution
abstract: Protein engineering requires navigating rugged fitness landscapes, where small sequence changes can produce large functional differences, but experimental screening can only sample a small fraction of sequence space. Thus, a central challenge is to efficiently traverse the large combinatorial space of mutations in silico. We introduce ProTEUS, a mutation-resolved world model for closed-loop protein evolution. Pretrained on deep mutational scanning assays, ProTEUS learns a joint representation of sequence, evolutionary, and structural information using MutationFormer, a mutation-biased attention architecture. Variants are represented as states in this joint latent space, and mutations define actions whose functional consequences are predicted. To support exploration of many mutants, we developed a fast, physics-constrained all-atom predictor that utilizes explicit geometric constraint enforcement to achieve >10 fold increase in speed than AlphaFold3 with guaranteed physical validity. Lastly, ProTEUS refines its prediction and understanding of protein activity through closed loop experimental feedback to guide evolution toward a desired phenotype. ProTEUS surpasses established models in both zero-shot and supervised fine-tuning mutation prediction tasks. We experimentally demonstrate its utility in two closed-loop multi-objective engineering campaigns on aldehyde dehydrogenase and levansucrase, yielding variants with >10 fold higher activity than wild type. ProTEUS provides a world-model framework that connects virtual evaluation of mutational outcomes with experimental learning for efficient protein evolution.

title: Optically modulated field-dependent electrical response in a non-collinear antiferromagnet/ferromagnet heterostructure
abstract: The interplay among optical, electrical, and magnetic stimuli offers opportunities to control the functional response of spintronic heterostructures. Here, we investigate the field-dependent electrical response of MgO/IrMn$_3$/Py/Au under radio-frequency (RF) excitation, white-light illumination, and direct-current (DC) bias. Under a 20 MHz RF signal with a nominal power of 2 W, the measured voltage in the dark remains at several tens of nanovolts. Upon illumination with approximately 1 W of white light, a pronounced field-dependent feature emerges around 315--320 Oe, reaching 0.9--1.0 $μ$V. The illumination-associated differential voltage is approximately 0.95 $μ$V. A DC current of 1 mA produces a response of approximately 1 $μ$V, while the simultaneous application of RF, DC, and optical excitation increases the voltage to approximately 1.8 $μ$V. Magnetic characterization reveals exchange bias with a blocking temperature near 380 K, while electrical resistance measurements show a pronounced dependence on magnetic-field orientation, consistent with the anisotropic response of the heterostructure. These results demonstrate that the field-dependent electrical response can be modulated through combined optical and electrical excitation, involving magneto-optical interactions and spin-dependent transport phenomena, potentially including spin Hall-related contributions and the magnetic spin Hall effect. This work provides insights into coupled optical, electrical, and magnetic-field effects in heterostructures based on non-collinear antiferromagnets and ferromagnetic layers.

title: Ultrafast Hole Transport and Electron Localization in Superatomic Re$_{6}$Se$_{8}$Cl$_{2}$
abstract: Van der Waals superatomic crystals represent an intriguing class of materials, exhibiting unique ultrafast electronic and structural responses arising from their hierarchical crystal structure. These materials bridge the properties of semiconductors, molecular solids, and nanocrystal arrays, hosting a range of many-body interactions that can be controlled with atomically precise structures. To establish the structure-function correlation, it is necessary to understand element-specific electronic states arising from complex superatomic unit cells. Here, we use transient XUV spectroscopy to individually probe the dynamics of photoexcited electrons and holes in Re$_{6}$Se$_{8}$Cl$_{2}$ superatomic crystals. We simultaneously measure photodynamics at the Re O$_{2}$ and Se M$_{4,5}$ edges, enabling decomposition of excited-state dynamics into the contributions of electron, hole, band gap, and phonon dynamics occurring around Re and Se atoms. By correlating spectral features at the Re and Se edges, we infer the existence of flat conduction bands and identify hot hole transfer from Re to Se atoms. We observe phonon oscillations driven by hole-mediated displacive excitations. The measurements highlight that the photodynamics are dominated by charge transfer between metallic sites which drives phonon coupling in the nonequilibrium state. This work provides insights into the optoelectronic applications of superatomic crystals for future tuning of emergent material properties.

title: A Perspective on Topological Charge Density Wave Materials
abstract: Charge density waves are among the earliest known ordered states in quantum materials, yet they have re-emerged at the center of modern discussions of topology, symmetry breaking, and collective dynamics. In several material classes, charge-density-wave order reshapes electronic bands, boundary states, defect structures, and electromagnetic responses in ways that invite a topological interpretation. Real-space imaging has shown that incommensurate order can form networks of phase defects rather than uniform modulations. Boundary-resolved spectroscopy has revealed in-gap modes whose existence and spatial structure track the charge-density-wave order, although such observations remain confined to a single material family. In Weyl materials, density-wave gaps have been linked to axion-like magnetoelectric response, placing the charge-density-wave phase within a dynamical-field description of the effective action. In kagome metals, charge order is intertwined with Berry curvature, unconventional symmetry breaking, and superconductivity. These developments have led to the term "topological charge density wave," but the phrase describes several physically distinct phenomena. We distinguish three meanings: (i) topology of the order parameter and its defects, (ii) topology of the charge-density-wave-reconstructed electronic structure and its boundary modes, and (iii) axion-like electromagnetic response generated by density-wave order. The experimental and theoretical support for these three meanings differs substantially. This Perspective traces the development of these ideas, clarifies the evidence behind each class, identifies unresolved questions and points of debate, and outlines experimental criteria for establishing topology in charge-density-wave states.

title: TASCopilot: A provenance-preserving assistant for triple-axis neutron scattering
abstract: Experimental decisions often depend on evidence scattered across papers, instrument logs, data files, and specialist software. A scientific assistant must connect that evidence without turning a plausible interpretation into an unsupported conclusion. TAS Co-pilot addresses this problem for triple-axis spectroscopy (TAS), which uses neutrons to probe material structure and excitations. It preserves provenance: the sources, processing steps, and review decisions behind each result. Independently maintained scientific tools communicate through structured requests and results; validation rules and human review govern how evidence can support a claim. Language models extract information and explain outcomes but do not approve scientific claims or control the instrument. Dependency-aware reduction executes existing scientific routines and reuses unchanged intermediate results. A retrospective SrMn$_2$Sb$_2$ study connects literature on a related material and historical alignment records to modeling of magnetic excitations in 20 measured scans. A live BT-7 study uses a dedicated instrument interface for fine alignment and 40 adaptively selected measurements. Agreement with a conventional measurement of the same crystal at shared conditions supports the acquisition and analysis chain. These cases demonstrate a methodology for maintaining inspectable evidence across literature, numerical analysis, and measurement at a user facility.

title: Multicomponent Isotope Engineering of Phonon Polaritons in Hexagonal Boron Nitride
abstract: Isotopic enrichment provides a non-invasive means of tuning the vibrational and optical properties of van der Waals crystals (vdW) without altering their lattice structure. We investigate two doubly enriched hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) compositions, h10B15N and h11B15N, to determine how isotope substitution on both sublattices modifies mid-infrared hyperbolic phonon polaritons (HPhPs). Polarization-resolved room temperature and cryogenic far-field reflectance measurements reveal optical-phonon blue shifts of approximately 35 cm-1 in h10B15N relative h11B15N, translating both Reststrahlen bands (RBs) and their polariton dispersions. For the upper RB, the combined accessible range expands from 1360-1614 cm-1 in natural hBN to 1356-1640 cm-1 across the B- enriched 14N crystals and 1339-1640 cm-1 when the 15N enriched crystals are included. Near-field imaging confirms deeply sub-diffractional propagation and shows that both crystals exhibit lower polariton damping and longer lifetimes than natural hBN, with performance comparable to monoisotopically enriched crystals. Further, we compare the conventional reduced-mass description with a phenomenological two-component inverse-mass model that captures the isotope dependence of the phonon frequencies and LO-TO coupling while resolving the contributions of the individual sublattices. These results establish multicomponent isotope engineering as a materials design strategy for positioning the HPhPs spectral range while preserving low-loss propagation in polar vdW crystals.

title: Agent-Guided Discovery of Exchange-Correlation Functionals with Physics-based Validation
abstract: Accurate, compact exchange--correlation functionals are central to predictive density functional theory. Symbolic search and language-model agents can propose new functional forms, but it remains unclear whether their gains survive self-consistency and external evaluation, whether the new terms carry physical content, whether agents outperform evolutionary search, and how language-model backbones compare. We connect frontier LLM agents to a GPU evaluator through the Model Context Protocol, with training-only fitting, persistent memory, and self-consistent and external evaluation. Opus-5.5 agents passed the screening gate with about 40-fold fewer tokens than Codex (GPT-6-Astra) agents and found a candidate with lower validation and held-out errors; only this candidate advanced to self-consistent evaluation. The resulting 13-parameter functional, O159, multiplies same-spin correlation by a smooth density window. Refitted controls favor a window that scales the entire same-spin factor, reducing it by 15--30\% at its peak, and that acts on reaction energies mainly in near-iso-orbital regions; against a refitted no-window control, it lowers heavy-atom total-energy errors on GSCDB137 by 29\%. With about 400 fits each, SyFES evolution did not improve on its GAS22 seed, whereas the agents found forms 0.10--0.13 \kcal\ lower in validation error by adding an explicit density scale. Self-consistent O159 lowers the held-out MGCDB84 test error of $ω$B97M-V by 11.7\%, and its mean normalized error ratio on 36 GSCDB137 datasets (1.139) is comparable to $ω$B97M-V (1.144) and below GAS22 (1.190). Frontier-LLM agents thus produced O159, a compact functional whose improvement over $ω$B97M-V survives self-consistent, physics-based validation.

title: Uncovered: Plastic pyrolysis
abstract: C&EN staffers probe a controversial way to deal with plastic waste
authors: Jeremy Barr, special to C&EN, Craig Bettenhausen, Leigh Krietsch Boerner, Alexander Tullo

title: Three RNA Vaccine Formats and the Lipid Problem Underneath Them
abstract: Six years after the first licensed mRNA vaccine, the argument in the field is no longer whether RNA can be delivered. It is which RNA, for how long, and at what cost in reactogenicity. Three molecular formats carry most of the work now: nucleoside-modified linear mRNA, self-amplifying RNA (saRNA) and circular RNA (circRNA). Each has produced human or near-human data since 2021, and each is limited at a different step-cytosolic lifetime, innate sensing of replication intermediates, and manufacturing.

title: FT-NIR Spectroscopy and Explainable Machine Learning for Eggshell Based Classification of Organic and Conventional Market Eggs
abstract: The premium pricing of organic eggs creates incentives for product misrepresentation and motivates the development of rapid, non-destructive screening tools to differentiate labeled organic and conventional eggs. Fourier transform near-infrared (FT-NIR) spectroscopy coupled with machine learning was evaluated for classifying retail eggs marketed as organic versus conventional. A total of 147 eggs were measured and spectra were analyzed using partial least squares–discriminant analysis (PLS-DA), along with gradient-boosted tree models (XGBoost and LightGBM).

title: An Embedded Plasticization Strategy for Flexible Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence Polymers with High Luminance
abstract: Thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) polymers offer the theoretical advantage of achieving 100% internal quantum efficiency. Together with their solution processability, TADF polymers are promising candidates for flexible display technologies. However, emissive polymers that simultaneously combine efficient TADF emission with mechanical flexibility remain rare. Here, we report an embedded plasticized linker strategy for mechanically compliant TADF polymers.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Dissecting the Influence of Molecular Charge on Hydrophobicity
abstract: Interactions of hydrophobic environments and ionic solutes are important in a range of biological processes, but the effect of molecular charge on hydrophobicity remains opaque. The interaction of isostructural solutes with the hydrophobic cavity of a cyclodextrin (γ-CD) in water was used to directly compare the hydrophobicities of anionic, neutral, and cationic species. Complex formation between γ-CD and PPh4+, BPh4– and a neutral analogue (CPh4 derivative) was investigated by ITC and NMR spectroscopy at different temperatures. The anion and neutral analogue bind γ-CD with similar association constants, but binding of the cation is 104-fold weaker. The thermodynamic signatures ΔH° and ΔCp° are similar for the anion and neutral analogue, but quite different for the cation. There is almost perfect entropy-enthalpy compensation in all three cases, but binding of the anion and neutral analogue is enthalpy-driven, while binding of the cation is entropy-driven. Substituents increase the affinity of tetraarylborates (up to 108 M–1, the highest reported value for native cyclodextrins), and substituent effects correlate well with the Hansch hydrophobicity parameter. In reversed-phase HPLC experiments that provide an alternative measure of hydrophobicity, the behavior of BPh4– is again similar to CPh4 and quite different from PPh4+, which is less retained by hydrophobic stationary phases. Asymmetry in the behavior of ions has implications for understanding partition coefficients of charged compounds, dipole potentials in lipid membranes, and the chaotropic effect. The experiments indicate that aqueous solvation of organic cations is much stronger than that of organic anions (by >20 kJ mol–1 for tetraphenyl compounds).
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Hybridization-brightened interlayer excitons in multilayer WSe2 controlled by sliding ferroelectricity
abstract: Interlayer excitons (IXs) combine spatially separated electron and hole wavefunctions with electrically tunable dipole moments, but their reduced wavefunction overlap generally limits optical emission, particularly for high-energy states. Here we report a bright, spectrally narrow high-energy interlayer exciton (h-IX) near 2.23 eV in few-layer WSe2 and investigate how its optical activity evolves with layer number and sliding-ferroelectric polarization. In pristine 2H-WSe2, we observe thickness-dependent brightening of high-energy exciton emission. GW-BSE calculations reveal mixed intralayer and interlayer configurations with enhanced optical weight, suggesting that multilayer hybridization contributes to the observed brightening. In parallel-stacked 3L/3L WSe2 containing a sliding-ferroelectric interface, the h-IX exhibits polarization-dependent energies and Stark responses that distinguish Pup and Pdown domains. Electric-field-driven domain-wall motion produces hysteretic transfer of spectral weight between the two h-IX branches, enabling optical tracking of ferroelectric switching. These results establish multilayer hybridization as a route to optically active high-energy interlayer excitons and sliding ferroelectricity as a complementary degree of freedom for controlling their energy, dipole and emission.

title: Curie's Jarvis: Autonomous Robotic Chemistry Experiments from Printed Protocols
abstract: A person running a bench experiment works from a printed instruction sheet, tells identical containers apart by the labels written on them, and looks at the bench again before each step. Lab automation usually works the other way around: the procedure is written as a script, and containers stand at fixed positions or carry fiducial markers. We present Curie's Jarvis, a system that lets a robot arm carry out a chemistry experiment on a bench set up for people. It reads the steps from a photo of the printed sheet, finds containers on an ordinary bench with no fixed positions or markers, tells identical-looking containers apart by reading their labels in four camera views, locates its target again before every step, and sets how each step is carried out, including its speed, from what is being handled. On a Franka Panda arm, Curie's Jarvis completed 5 of 5 runs of one protocol from a children's chemistry kit and 4 of 5 runs of another, with no human intervention, and in 160 locates on printed and handwritten labels it identified every container correctly. This brings robots a step closer to doing bench chemistry the way people do.

title: W-ISA: Transactional Execution of Weight-Space Intervention Programs
abstract: We present W-ISA, a software instruction set and transactional runtime for executing weight-space intervention programs on pretrained language models. Shape-checked instructions express parameter updates, projections, ablations, and rank-one transformations. The runtime applies these programs within request-scoped execution contexts and restores saved parameters after completion or interruption. Activation-based match-action rules connect measured model states to intervention selection. We evaluate restoration and replay on SmolLM-135M-Instruct and Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, and compare materialized rank-one updates with equivalent PyTorch hooks on the latter. In 45 timed requests, both intervention implementations produce identical greedy sequences at 32, 128, and 512 tokens; their maximum prompt-logit difference is 0.000184. On the complete WikiText-2 raw test split, the combined SmolLM attention-head ablation and MLP projection changes perplexity from 22.2353 to 22.3188, a relative increase of 0.3754%. W-ISA separates intervention specification, execution, and measurement, making parameter-level experiments reproducible and composable.

title: Characterization of inter-antibody variability in clinical pharmacokinetics of monoclonal antibodies using low-dimensional neural ordinary differential equations (NODE)
abstract: Monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) exhibit high inter-antibody variability in clinical pharmacokinetics (PK), influenced by both molecular and physiological factors. Traditional models, including PBPK and TMDD frameworks, provide mechanistic detail but can be computationally intensive and limited in their ability to generalize across diverse antibodies. Neural ordinary differential equations (NODEs) represent a flexible, low-dimensional alternative that combines mechanistic interpretability with machine learning adaptability.

title: Reweighting Free Energy Profiles with Universal Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials for Fast Consensus Building
abstract: Universal machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) have made density functional theory (DFT)-level molecular dynamics highly affordable. However, their rapid proliferation makes it prohibitively expensive to benchmark every new model against the potential of mean force (PMF), the bridge between microscopic atomic fluctuations and macroscopic thermodynamic and kinetic observables.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: EvoSurv: Evolution-Aware Multimodal Survival Modeling Reveals Complementary Prognostic Signals
abstract: Accurate cancer survival prediction remains challenging due to tumor heterogeneity. Although multimodal survival models integrate clinical and molecular data, they often overlook evolutionary information encoded in genomic alterations. To address this gap, we developed eTime, a 38-dimensional evolutionary representation comprising eight feature groups that characterize clonal and subclonal mutation burden, mutational spectra, functional consequences, copy-number alterations, and anoikis-related genomic changes. We further developed EvoSurv, a multimodal survival framework integrating eTime with clinical variables and RNA expression. Across six TCGA cancer cohorts comprising 2,782 patients, EvoSurv achieved the highest mean concordance index (C-index) in all six cancers, averaging 0.663 and outperforming three state-of-the-art survival prediction methods. More importantly, we assessed whether evolutionary features provide additional prognostic information beyond clinical and transcriptomic predictors. eTime remained significantly associated with survival in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSC) and liver hepatocellular carcinoma (LIHC) after adjustment for clinical variables and RNA-derived risk scores. Feature-group analyses further revealed cancer-specific prognostic patterns. In HNSC, T>G substitutions were associated with increased mortality risk after clinical and molecular adjustment, including in HPV-negative patients, with supporting evidence from an independent CPTAC-HNSCC cohort. Overall, these findings demonstrate that eTime captures survival-associated evolutionary information and highlight its potential to provide prognostic value beyond clinical and transcriptomic predictors.

title: Thermodynamically consistent neural constitutive models for elastoplasticity via eigen-representations
abstract: Neural network material models can represent yield surfaces and hardening laws with far more flexibility than classical closed-form plasticity formulations, but training such a model end-to-end through an implicit return map introduces non-trivial challenges. This work presents a thermodynamically consistent neural constitutive model for rate-independent, isotropic elastoplasticity that jointly learns a flexible yield function together with its evolution laws. For non-associative flow, the yield function extends the convex flow potential by a jointly trained additive term, which renders the model thermodynamically consistent by construction. Isotropy and convexity are enforced simultaneously across all learnable components through a permutation-invariant, spectral (eigenvalue-based) representation. Training proceeds through a backward-Euler return map, with gradients propagated by the implicit function theorem together with an eigenvalue-degeneracy-aware scheme for safe differentiation. The robustness and generality of the approach are demonstrated by reproducing known constitutive models, including non-associative flow, learning material behavior from stress--strain data extracted from a full-field finite element simulation, and capturing unknown non-associative behavior from homogenized representative volume elements of a foam. Finally, the proposed neural plasticity model is evaluated within finite element simulations to solve boundary-value-problem under plane stress.

title: Autonomous Optimization of Numerical Algorithms by an AI Agent: Application to Atomistic Simulation
abstract: Coding agents built on large language models, run in automated improvement loops, can discover more efficient algorithms. We present AIOA, a framework that brings this approach to the numerical algorithms of atomistic simulation: an agent improves an algorithm against a pre-specified metric in a loop guarded by verifiers it cannot alter. Applied to ASE, a widely used atomistic simulation library, AIOA targets two facets of an algorithm: its implementation, rewritten to run faster with unchanged results, and the method itself, redesigned to converge with fewer force evaluations. Agents made six kernels 22-24 times faster on average in Python with NumPy and SciPy. On unseen problems, optimizers from the best configuration needed 3.1-3.4 times fewer force evaluations than L-BFGS for structure relaxation and 4.6-17 times fewer than standard climbing-image nudged elastic band calculations for reaction paths. The agents' optimizers also contain two algorithmic components we did not find in the literature.

title: Interpretable Machine Learning Accelerated Discovery of Doped Spinel Co3O4 Catalysts for the Oxygen Evolution Reaction
abstract: The discovery of doped spinel Co3O4 electrocatalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is hindered by the large catalyst design space and the high computational cost of density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Here, we establish a hierarchical interpretable machine learning (ML) framework that decouples electronic structure prediction from catalytic activity prediction. By starting with predicting the electronic descriptor (d-band center) from readily accessible structural descriptors and subsequently predicting adsorption energetics, the framework removes the need for expensive electronic structure DFT calculations during catalyst screening while preserving physical interpretability. A random forest model was trained on adsorption free energies of OH*, O*, and OOH* from 144 representative active sites and achieved a test mean absolute error of 0.21 eV. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis identified surface energy, active site undercoordination, and the d-band center as the dominant descriptors governing adsorption energetics. To avoid additional DFT calculations of the d-band center during screening, a second ML model predicted it directly from structural and elemental descriptors with a test mean absolute error of 0.23 eV. The resulting framework enabled rapid evaluation of OER overpotentials across 252 active sites, while subsequent targeted DFT calculations identified Al-, Ca-, Fe-, and Mn-doped Co3O4 as promising candidates. Targeted DFT calculations and electrochemical measurements further validated the improved OER activity of Al- and Fe-doped Co3O4. This work establishes an interpretable and computationally efficient strategy for connecting structural descriptors, electronic properties, adsorption energetics, and experimentally measurable catalytic activity, thereby accelerating the discovery of high-performance spinel oxide catalysts.

title: Beyond the Document: Compiled Context and Governed Agents for Any Work Product
abstract: A document preserves the visible result of professional work but often discards the research, calculations, assumptions, evidence, and authorization boundaries behind it. We study a different unit of delivery: a Portable Agent Format (PAF) package that carries a work product together with compiled context, evidence, provenance, and rules for subsequent interaction. To test whether this context remains useful beyond the process that produced it, we evaluate four new packages, created after the hosted and offline readers were fixed: an investment proposal, fund research, financial-statement analysis, and an engineering incident review. Two packages were produced by specialized agents and two through a general-purpose assistant's packaging skill. Across 400 frozen questions and 12,000 evaluated responses, a hosted governed reader succeeds on 96% of questions versus 86% with instructions plus raw-file retrieval (Holm-adjusted p < 10^-7). On the 260 answerable questions per condition, success is 94% versus 79%; the gap varies by package. Source-material chat and instructions alone reach 48% and 74% overall. A separate 0.8-billion-parameter offline reader succeeds on 69% overall, but 54% on answerable questions. Its -1 response rate is 2.9%, combining materially wrong and unauthorized answers, versus 56% with the source and instructions alone. Ablations suggest advantages for the integrated selector and package-adapted writer, without isolating representation from training effects. The same run exposes a failure: offline retrieval resolves none of the 40 historical-record questions in one financial-data package. These findings support treating compiled knowledge as part of the delivered work product, while leaving independent standards interoperability and end-to-end governance conformance unproven.

title: Point defects and primary radiation damage in Co-free Fe-Ni-Cr-Mn high-entropy alloys from molecular dynamics
abstract: Co-free Fe-Ni-Cr-Mn high-entropy alloys (HEAs) are candidates for nuclear structural applications. We used molecular dynamics with the EAM-21 potential, stiffened at short range, to study five HEAs that have been irradiated experimentally: Fe37Ni34Cr16Mn13 (ES1), Fe35Ni35Cr15Mn15 (P35), Fe46Ni22Cr15Mn17 (Y3), Fe27Ni28Cr18Mn27 (Kumar) and Fe30Ni30Cr10Mn30 (C30). They were compared with pure Ni, Fe60Ni40, the Fe70Ni10Cr20 model alloy of 316L, and Fe50Ni34Cr16, which is ES1 with Mn replaced by Fe. We calculated stacking fault energies, threshold displacement energies, point-defect formation and migration energies, and 1015 displacement cascades from 5 to 40 keV at 300 and 823 K. The stacking fault energy follows the Ni content: 19-44 mJ/m^2 in the alloys and 113 mJ/m^2 in Ni. Compared with the Mn-free alloys, the HEAs have lower threshold displacement energies (48-56 against 64-74 eV) and lower dumbbell formation energies, and Mn is the element most transported by interstitials. All the concentrated alloys leave about the same number of Frenkel pairs, 56-72 at 40 keV, half the number in Ni. At 40 keV, 54-58% of the interstitials are in clusters in the HEAs, against 67-71% in Fe60Ni40, Fe70Ni10Cr20 and Fe50Ni34Cr16 and 82% in Ni. At the same cluster size, clusters of 4-12 interstitials are faulted about half as often in the HEAs, and this does not follow the stacking fault energy. The surviving interstitials are enriched in Mn in the HEAs and in Ni in the Mn-free alloys, and depleted in Cr. The results support direct loop formation in cascades in Fe60Ni40 and Fe70Ni10Cr20 and less of it in ES1.

title: Ion-Pair Receptors Couple Cation Binding with Molecular Electron Storage for Room-Temperature Birch-Type Reduction
abstract: The Birch reduction provides a powerful route to partially dearomatized products from aromatic precursors, but classical protocols rely on highly reactive solvated electrons generated from alkali metals in cryogenic liquid ammonia, offering limited molecular control over reducing equivalents. Here we show that ion-pair receptors couple Na+ binding with molecular electron storage within electron-deficient diimide-based π-frameworks.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Nontargeted metabolomics-based discrimination of the geographical origin of Pteridium aquilinum using liquid chromatography-high-resolution mass spectrometry and machine learning
abstract: BackgroundDistinguishing the geographical origins of agricultural products is essential for food safety, quality, and consumer protection. In this study, nontargeted metabolomics based on liquid chromatography-quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry was leveraged to distinguish bracken (Pteridium aquilinum) originating from South Korea and China.ResultsA total of 109 samples were analyzed, and 333 features were identified. Based on the fold-change and t-test analyses, a volcano plot was constructed, revealing the differences among constituent metabolites.
venue: Journal of the science of food and agriculture

title: Mitsui Chemicals will acquire JSR in electronic materials push
abstract: The deal is the largest ever in Japan’s chemical industry and advances restructuring of the sector

title: Kolmogorov-Chapman Maps: Trajectory-Free Learning for Simulating Molecular Dynamics
abstract: Stochastic differential equations (SDEs) describe stochastic processes across a wide range of scientific domains, including physics, biology, and finance. Although individual numerical integration steps are inexpensive, observing meaningful events or transitions can require millions of sequential steps, resulting in substantial wall-clock simulation time and poor hardware utilization. Deep learning offers an alternative by amortizing many integration steps into a single neural network forward pass, potentially enabling much faster simulation. However, existing supervised approaches typically require long simulated trajectory data, which restricts their applicability. In this work, we introduce Kolmogorov-Chapman Maps (KC-Maps), a method for learning the transition kernel of an SDE that relies only on the trajectory-free marginal samples together with the known drift and diffusion coefficients. Given an initial time and state of a process, KC-Maps models its distribution integrated to any given time, corresponding to the weak solution of the SDE. To recover the correct dynamics, KC-Maps satisfies two key properties: (i) it satisfies the boundary conditions, which we incorporate directly into the neural network architecture, and (ii) it respects the Kolmogorov--Chapman equation, which provides an efficient training objective. We empirically demonstrate that KC-Maps learns to integrate the dynamics of peptide molecular systems and outperforms classical molecular dynamics in terms of GPU-hours.

title: High Pressure Material Phase Identification with Gaussian Kernel Neural Networks
abstract: Phase identification is a computational task involving the classification of material structure using the positions of atoms. Using data from Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations, our task is to identify the material phase of a set of atoms, based on how the simulations predict their positioning relative to each other. By leveraging existing research on mechanistic neural network theory, particularly Neural Tangent Kernels (NTK), we develop a new and efficient method for classifying simulated material samples. Our method involves defining a set of "atom detectors" that are given positions around the origin in cartesian coordinates. The sum of Gaussians centered at each atom is calculated at each atom detector, and is used as the input to a neural network. We present theoretical and experimental evidence to show that this method is highly effective and efficient at the task. Our method obtains better or similar accuracy scores to commonly used methods while having a major computational speedup.

title: UniHam: A Large-Scale SOC-Complete Dataset and Benchmark for Hamiltonian Learning in Materials
abstract: Accurate prediction of electronic Hamiltonians would enable broad property inference while avoiding the high computational cost of Density Functional Theory (DFT). However, progress toward general-purpose materials foundation models is limited by a data bottleneck: existing Hamiltonian datasets are typically small, lack structural diversity, and often omit essential relativistic physics such as spin--orbit coupling (SOC). We therefore construct UniHam, a large-scale Hamiltonian dataset and benchmark suite comprising 100,000+ DFT-computed complex-valued Hermitian Hamiltonians with full SOC, covering 72 elements and a wide range of crystal geometries and symmetries (spanning diverse lattice types and space-group families). Building on UniHam, we benchmark two representative state-of-the-art models under a standardized protocol and introduce complementary evaluation metrics that jointly assess three dimensions: (i) Hamiltonian reconstruction accuracy, (ii) out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization across composition/symmetry shifts, and (iii) the ability to support downstream property prediction from the predicted Hamiltonians. Experiments on UniHam demonstrate that the proposed benchmark and metrics effectively differentiate model capabilities, revealing intrinsic SOC- and element-dependent failure modes, large variations in compositional OOD robustness, and the necessity of spectral-level evaluation to assess whether Hamiltonian predictions reliably support downstream electronic-structure properties. Overall, UniHam provides a reproducible, SOC-complete benchmark that can sharpen model comparisons and accelerate the development of next-generation foundation models for quantum materials.

title: Pd Single-Atom Engineered Janus BiOCl/MXene Heterostructure for Printed Self-Decoupled Temperature-Humidity Dual-Mode Sensors
abstract: The advancement of flexible sensing technologies is of paramount importance in biomedical engineering. However, achieving high-fidelity multi-modal temperature-humidity sensing without inter-channel cross-talk and computational post-processing remains a formidable challenge due to overlapping transduction mechanisms. In this study, an unprecedented electron-ion synergistic functional material, featuring a unique inherent self-decoupling capability, was developed based on the Janus hierarchical heterostructure.

title: Consistency, Cancellation, and Experiment in Quasi-Harmonic Thermochemistry
abstract: For weakly bound molecular complexes, the Gibbs energy is often limited less by the electronic interaction energy, now computed to near chemical accuracy, than by the statistical-mechanical treatment of their low-frequency intermolecular vibrations. The standard remedy, Grimme’s quasi-harmonic correction, rescales the entropy of these modes toward a free-rotor limit while leaving their energy harmonic; because both derive from the same partition function, this is thermodynamically inconsistent.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: MechFoundry: An agentic loop that poses and performs engineering analyses and optimization of real-world objects
abstract: AI agents can automate software engineering because a compiler or a test suite checks that the code does what the user or the agent intended. In engineering analysis, however, the steps that precede the computation have few easily verifiable checks: modeling a design or an object, deciding how it is used, where supports and loads are applied, and what material each part is made of. A human expert therefore makes these decisions, carries out the steps, and judges the result, one object at a time. We present MechFoundry, an agentic loop coupled with bespoke software that automates structural analyses of real-world objects without a human in the loop. From an object's lexical description, it generates a shape, poses a loading case relevant to how the object is used, assigns a material to each part, solves the nonlinear structural response, and improves the design against the loads it carries. A differentiable GPU solver built on an adaptive octree that need not conform to the surface enables the transition from shape generation to simulation and optimization. Across 50 everyday and engineering objects, the agent posed and solved a loading case in 6.5 minutes and for US$1.3 per object on average. Without a test suite to check against, we had language-model reviewers grade each session, as a first indication of where the agent's engineering judgment holds and where it fails.

title: Deep learning-guided discovery reveals the diversity and mutational potential of environmental beta-lactamases
abstract: Beta-lactamases are a major mechanism of bacterial resistance to beta-lactam antibiotics; however, their functional diversity and mutational potential in environmental microbial communities remain partially understood. This study aimed to characterize environmental beta-lactamase diversity and investigate how sequence variation influences antibiotic resistance. By integrating protein language model (PLMs) with ensemble learning, we identified more than 46,000 putative beta-lactamases across all four Ambler classes from environmental metagenomes, widely distributed across diverse habitats, with distinct habitat-associated class compositions. The candidates sharing approximately 30% sequence identity with known beta-lactamases conferred resistance to multiple beta-lactam antibiotics when expressed in Escherichia coli. Combining inverse folding model with PLMs further identified mutations that altered resistance profiles, including substitutions that increased resistance to carbapenems. Predicted high-fitness sites exhibited greater natural sequence variability overall, with higher variability in wastewater-derived than ocean-derived enzymes. These findings reveal undercharacterized beta-lactamase diversity and substantial mutational flexibility in environmental microbiomes, providing a basis for investigating their potential contribution to the diversification of antibiotic resistance.

title: Monomer Flexibility Enables the Regulation of Interlayer Stacking in Two-Dimensional Covalent Organic Frameworks
abstract: Precise control over interlayer stacking in two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (2D COFs) remains far less developed than the design of in-plane topology. Here, rather than regulating stacking through external changes in the crystallization medium, we investigate the conformational compatibility of paired monomers as an internal molecular variable for directing the out-of-plane organization of 2D COFs. A topologically related series of eight imine-linked COFs was constructed using different combinations of flexible and rigid monomers.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Integrated Multi-omics Reveals Molecular Signatures of Rett Syndrome, Informing Future Biomarker Discovery
abstract: Rett syndrome (RTT) is a severe neurodevelopmental disorder primarily caused by pathogenic variants in the X-linked methyl-CpG-binding protein 2 (MECP2) gene. Despite numerous clinical trials being conducted, there are limited disease-modifying options available for individuals with RTT. This paucity of effective treatments can in part be attributed to the lack of clinically useful biomarkers that can objectively assess treatment response. Moreover, diagnosis of RTT continues to be clinical, when clinical manifestations are apparent, precluding early therapeutic approaches. Thus, clinical biomarkers of disease stage could improve diagnosis and enable real-time monitoring of response to treatment, providing the earliest possible indications of therapeutic efficacy. Given MeCP2's role as a key regulator of gene transcription, we used an untargeted omics approach to evaluate transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolic profiles in blood from individuals with RTT (n = 9) and age- and sex-matched controls (n = 8). In addition to characterising differential expression at each omic layer, to understand the shared biology and coordinated molecular signals across all omic datasets, we used the unsupervised machine learning framework Multi-Omics Factor Analysis version 2 (MOFA2). The individual omic data consisted of a robust upregulation of genes involved in ribosomal structure and translation together with a downregulation in vesicle trafficking genes. An upregulation in ribosomal machinery and mitochondrial function together with a concomitant downregulation of critical epigenetic regulators, immune-signalling molecules, and cytoskeletal structural anchors was observed in the proteomics, which was supported by the phosphoproteomics. Notably, plasma metabolomics pointed towards alterations in energy substrates and lipid/cholesterol handling, suggesting systemic downstream consequences of primary intracellular disturbances. The integrated MOFA2 data supported the individual omic data revealing a central disease axis principally shaped by the proteome and transcriptome and supported by the metabolome and phosphoproteome, identifying potential biomarkers, including latent biological processes that distinguish RTT from controls (Latent Factor 1) and correlates of clinical severity (Latent Factor 2). Overall, our data reveal a distinctive 'disease state' molecular signature that distinguishes individuals with RTT from controls, where the findings in RTT blood cells are consistent with previously reported altered translational and mitochondrial function and disrupted chromatin regulation, cytoskeletal dynamics, and metabolic signalling. Our integrated multi-omics analyses revealed that PBMC's LTN1, ATRX, CHD8, SPTB, DMTN, PRF1, CD40LG, and PTPRCAP and plasma glutamate are the most promising disease-state (complementary diagnostic) candidate biomarkers while sphingomyelin, RTN3, and MMP1 appear to be the most suitable biomarkers of disease severity. Here, we demonstrate that blood from individuals with RTT reflects the molecular systemic consequences of MeCP2 dysfunction.
